For concurrency capture dependencies rather than relying on sleeps to force an order. Test boundary cases such as empty input, one element, allocation failure and interrupted I/O. Keep a failure’s minimal reproduction and verify the intended invariant after fixing the cause.
topics.formula:
Mnemonic: reproduce → localize → explain → change → verify
Boundary set: zero, one, last valid, first invalid, resource failure
Evidence rule: no observed failure ≠ proof that no failure exists
topics.symbols: The sequence describes an investigation workflow, not a formal algorithm with a fixed runtime. Last valid and first invalid refer to a precisely stated bound, such as array length or buffer capacity. Resource failure includes allocation, opening, thread creation and interrupted operations where the API can report them. A tool result is limited to the executed path, configuration and its detection capabilities. Verification should target the repaired invariant and related edge cases, while avoiding undefined behavior in the test’s own expected-output reasoning.
topics.example: A line processor crashes only when an input has eight characters. Its buffer has capacity 8 and the copy stores all eight characters before appending a terminator at index 8. Valid indices are 0 through 7, so the first invalid write is the terminator. A memory checker may point to that store; the root cause is failing to reserve one byte. Repair by bounding the payload at seven characters or allocating nine bytes for this input, then define how longer lines are handled. Verify empty, seven-character, eight-character and longer inputs. A run that happened not to crash before the repair would not have made the out-of-bounds write valid.
topics.pitfall: Do not write tests that expect a particular value from signed overflow, a data race or freed memory. Undefined behavior has no portable expected result to assert.

check.question: Why can adding printf make a race appear to disappear?
check.answer: It changes timing, scheduling and sometimes synchronization inside the library. That can hide a symptom while leaving the original shared-state protocol incorrect.

cheatsheet.title: Representation is a contract
cheatsheet.body: Unsigned arithmetic wraps modulo its range; signed overflow is undefined. sizeof returns size_t in C bytes. Initialize automatic objects and match formatted-I/O conversions to actual argument types.

cheatsheet.title: Pointers need live bounds
cheatsheet.body: Array arithmetic stays within the array or its one-past position; never dereference the latter. A multidimensional array decays to a pointer to a row, not a pointer to pointer.

cheatsheet.title: Text needs capacity and termination
cheatsheet.body: Reserve strlen+1 bytes. Bounded reads can split a logical line. Check conversion results, suffixes and range; never treat arbitrary bytes as a terminated C string.

cheatsheet.title: Own every allocation
cheatsheet.body: Check n≤SIZE_MAX/sizeof(*p) before multiplying. Check allocation results, initialize before reading, preserve the old pointer on realloc failure and end all borrowing before one eventual free.

cheatsheet.title: Build stages differ
cheatsheet.body: Preprocessing expands tokens; compilation checks a translation unit; linking resolves external definitions. Headers describe interfaces. Macros can duplicate side effects, and include guards do not prevent cross-file multiple definitions.

cheatsheet.title: Signals need a minimal handler
cheatsheet.body: Prefer sigaction and async-signal-safe operations. A small stop flag can defer cleanup to normal flow. Use an atomic mask-and-wait protocol when checking a predicate and sleeping for signals.

cheatsheet.title: Process lifecycle
cheatsheet.body: fork duplicates execution with separate ordinary memory; exec replaces the image; waitpid collects status. Check each result, close unused inherited descriptors and decode wait status with its matching macros.

cheatsheet.title: Streams are not messages
cheatsheet.body: Pipes and stream sockets can split or combine writes across reads. Define framing and loop over partial transfers. Pipe EOF requires drained data and every write endpoint closed.

cheatsheet.title: Shared storage needs a protocol
cheatsheet.body: Shared memory removes some copying, not synchronization requirements. Use offsets across mappings. Semaphore permits track resources; mutexes protect invariants. Define initialization, shutdown and recovery ownership.

cheatsheet.title: Thread coordination
cheatsheet.body: Keep arguments alive through use and join created threads correctly. Protect every conflicting access. A condition wait belongs in a predicate loop with its mutex; volatile is not general synchronization.

cheatsheet.title: Prevent circular waits
cheatsheet.body: Acquire locks by stable global rank and include joins, condition waits and I/O in dependency analysis. A trylock loop can avoid blocking yet still livelock; timeouts alone do not diagnose deadlock.

cheatsheet.title: Measure equivalent work
cheatsheet.body: Speedup=T₁/Tp using elapsed time for the same verified result. Partition output ownership, combine after dependencies complete and account for serial work, bandwidth, imbalance and synchronization costs.
